metaTitle: Best Sliding Compound Miter Saws in 2026
metaDescription: Six sliding compound miter saws compared on crosscut width, rail design, dual bevel, crown capacity and cordless options for trim and framing.
expertTake: The Makita LS1219L is the sliding compound miter saw to buy for most trim shops, with a 2-rail single slide design, a 15 inch crosscut and 8 inch nested crown capacity. The Skil MS6305 is the value pick for a 10 inch dual bevel saw. If you only cut baseboard and casing, skip sliding saws and buy a fixed miter saw, since a slider needs more bench depth and costs far more.
introParagraphs: A sliding compound miter saw mounts the blade on rails so the head can travel forward and back, which lets a modest blade cut boards far wider than the blade itself. It is the saw for shelving, stair parts and wide crown moulding, but it demands more space and a careful setup.
This guide explains slide mechanisms, crosscut and crown capacity, dual bevel and cordless options, and why rail quality decides accuracy.

products.name: Makita LS1219L 12 Inch Dual-Bevel Sliding Compound Miter Saw with Laser
products.description:
The LS1219L uses a unique 2-rail steel sliding system with a single slide-glide operation, which cuts the saw's footprint compared with four rail designs. It crosscuts 15 inches at 90 degrees, and cuts up to 8 inch crown moulding nested and 6-3/4 inch baseboard standing vertically. A laser helps line up the blade and an in-front bevel lock makes bevel changes convenient.

Compared with the DeWalt DWS780 it has a simpler rail system and a bit more crosscut, while the DeWalt has the XPS shadow light. Against the 10 inch LS1019L it cuts wider boards and taller crown. It is the saw for professional trim and finish work.

Keep the rails clean and lubricated, and check the fence for square. Because the head travels on bearings, never let sawdust build up on the rails. Add a stand with support wings for long boards.
products.bestFor: Professional trim shops that cut wide stock and crown.

products.name: DeWalt DWS780 12 Inch Double Bevel Sliding Compound Miter Saw
products.description:
The DWS780 pairs a 15 amp, 3,800 rpm motor with a double bevel sliding head and the XPS LED shadow light, which projects the blade's shadow on the work for adjustment free accuracy. An integrated cutline blade positioning system keeps the indicator true. A blade wrench and material clamp come in the box.

Compared with the Makita LS1219L it has a four rail style slide that is bulkier, but it has the excellent shadow light. Against the cordless DCS785B it has more sustained power and no battery cost. It is a long time favorite of carpenters.

Keep the XPS light clear of dust and the rails lubricated. Check blade alignment every few months. Pair it with a dust bag or a vacuum to keep the shadow light clean.
products.bestFor: Carpenters who value the shadow line and a proven design.
pros: XPS shadow light needs no adjustment

products.name: DeWalt DCS785B 20V MAX XR 12 Inch Cordless Sliding Miter Saw
products.description:
The DCS785B is DeWalt's largest cordless miter saw, cutting up to 14 inches horizontally and 6-1/2 inch baseboard standing up. Regenerative braking captures energy to extend battery life. It runs on the full range of 20V MAX batteries and the FlexVolt line.

Compared with the corded DWS780 it gives up some sustained power but removes the cord, which suits jobsites without outlets. Against the Makita LS1219L it has a slightly smaller crosscut. It is a strong choice for trim contractors who move between rooms.

It is a bare tool, and large batteries make it more practical. Keep the rails clean. Keep the battery in a cool place and rotate packs on long days.
products.bestFor: Contractors who work on sites without convenient power.

products.name: Makita LS1019L 10 Inch Dual-Bevel Sliding Compound Miter Saw with Laser
products.description:
The LS1019L is a 10 inch slider with a crown molding capacity of 6-5/8 inches nested, equal to a 12 inch saw, thanks to a direct drive gearbox and guard design. A linear ball bearing system is engineered for dead-on accurate cuts, and vertical capacity is 5-1/4 inches. A laser helps with alignment.

Compared with the LS1219L it is smaller, lighter and cheaper, at the cost of crosscut width. Against the Skil MS6305 it has a more refined slide. It is a strong choice for remodelers who want portability.

Keep the ball bearing rails clean, and check the laser alignment. Replace the stock blade for fine work. Wipe the ball bearing rails with a dry cloth after dusty jobs.
products.bestFor: Remodelers who want pro accuracy in a lighter saw.
pros: Ball bearing slide for smooth accuracy
6-5/8 inch crown capacity from a 10 inch blade

products.name: Skil MS6305 10 Inch Dual Bevel Sliding Compound Miter Saw

specList.label: Bevel
specList.value: Dual, stops at 48 and 45 left, 0, 45 right

products.description:
The Skil MS6305 has a 15 amp motor at 4,800 rpm, a 10 inch blade and a dual bevel with four positive stops at 48 and 45 degrees left, 0 degrees and 45 degrees right. An LED shadow line gives more precision than a laser. It is a full featured slider at a modest price.

Compared with the Makita LS1019L it is less refined in the slide and costs less. Against the Dovaman 12 inch it has a smaller blade and a faster motor. It suits serious DIYers and light trim work.

Check the rails and fence for square at setup. Keep the shadow line lens clean. Keep the shadow line lens free of sawdust and finger marks.
products.bestFor: Serious DIYers who want a dual bevel slider on a budget.
pros: Dual bevel with four positive stops

products.name: Dovaman 12 Inch Dual-Bevel Sliding Compound Miter Saw
products.description:
The Dovaman 12 inch slider uses a 15 amp copper motor at 3,800 rpm and a dual bevel at 45 degrees each way, with a maximum cut of 4.2 inches by 13 inches. A laser guide aids accuracy. It offers 12 inch capacity at a budget price.

Compared with the Makita LS1219L it has a similar blade size but less refined rails. Against the Skil MS6305 it has a larger blade and a lower speed. It is a good value for shop projects.

Expect to check and adjust the fence and bevel out of the box. Treat the stock blade as a starter. Adjust the fence and bevel scale out of the box before you trust it.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists who want a 12 inch slider on a tight budget.
pros: 12 inch blade at a low price
cons: Needs setup checks out of the box

buyingCriteria.explanation: A sliding saw cuts wider than its blade, from 13 inches on the Dovaman to 15 inches on the Makita LS1219L and 14 inches on the DeWalt DCS785B. A 10 inch slider like the LS1019L cuts narrower boards. Choose capacity for the widest board you cut. A 12 inch slider covers most shelving and stair parts. A common mistake is to buy on the 15 inch headline and then discover that a 2x12 needs a deeper cut than the saw makes at an angle. Check the capacity at 45 degrees in the manual, since it is often several inches smaller than the 90 degree figure.

The slide mechanism decides accuracy over years. The Makita LS1219L uses two steel rails, and the LS1019L linear ball bearings. Four rail designs like the DeWalt's use more space. Check that the head glides without wobble. Rail systems that hide behind the saw save bench depth, and a long slide travel extends capacity without a bigger blade. Look for a smooth glide with no side to side play when you push the head by hand.

Dual bevel tilts both ways, so you do not flip stock for crown or compound cuts. All six saws here are dual bevel. It saves time on trim. Check the bevel lock is easy to reach. Dual bevel is a real time saver on crown, but it also needs a bevel lock you can reach with the board in place. A lock at the front of the saw, as on the Makita, is easier than one behind the head.

The Makita LS1219L cuts 8 inch crown nested and 6-3/4 inch baseboard vertical. The LS1019L cuts 6-5/8 inch crown. Taller stock needs larger saws. Check your trim before you buy. Crown is cut either nested against the fence or flat on the table with a bevel, and the saw's capacity limits which method you can use. A 12 inch saw with taller fence support handles larger crown profiles.

The DeWalt DCS785B is cordless, with regenerative braking, and the others are corded 15 amp saws. Corded saws hold power all day. Cordless saws suit sites without outlets. Consider battery cost. Cordless sliders spend battery fast on thick stock, so plan a spare large pack for a full day. Corded saws avoid that tradeoff but tie you to an outlet and an extension cord.

A shadow line, as on the DeWalt DWS780 and Skil, shows the blade path without adjustment. Lasers need alignment. Accuracy aids matter less than a square fence. Check out of the box. Shadow lines depend on good ambient light, and lasers on clean lenses. Neither replaces a test cut on scrap, so make one before every crown or compound cut.

specDecoder.watchFor: Check the spring angle. Crown size depends on the saw's fence height.

specDecoder.meaning: A slide using ball bearings for smooth, accurate glide, as on the Makita LS1019L.
specDecoder.watchFor: Keep it clean. Keep bearing rails dry and clean.

specDecoder.meaning: A head that tilts left and right for compound cuts.
specDecoder.watchFor: It adds weight. Bevel locks should be easy to reach.

specDecoder.meaning: A system that recovers energy when the blade slows, used on the DCS785B to extend battery life.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared crosscut, from 13 inches on the Dovaman to 15 inches on the LS1219L, plus crown and vertical capacity. We checked capacity at angles, not just at 90 degrees.

howWeEvaluated.title: Slide and build
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited rail systems, including the LS1219L's two steel rails and the LS1019L's ball bearings. Rail quality was weighed more than extras.

howWeEvaluated.title: Accuracy aids
howWeEvaluated.description: We rewarded shadow lines on the DWS780 and Skil, and lasers on the Makita saws. Dust control was noted but not weighted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 15 amp corded saws with the cordless DCS785B. Weight was compared with a stand in mind.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The LS1219L leads overall, the DWS780 for shadow line and the DCS785B for cordless. The LS1019L is the 10 inch pro, the Skil the value slider and the Dovaman the budget 12 inch. We ranked by use case, not a single winner.

cards.label: 10 inch
cards.text: Lighter and cheaper with good crown capacity. The Makita LS1019L and Skil MS6305 fit here.

cards.label: 12 inch
cards.text: Wider crosscut and taller stock. The Makita LS1219L, DeWalt DWS780, DCS785B and Dovaman fit here.

howToChoose.note: Choose 10 inch for portability and 12 inch for shelving and stair parts.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Dual bevel, nested crown capacity and accurate detents. Crown needs a precise spring angle. A shadow line helps.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Makita LS1219L cuts 8 inch crown nested. The LS1019L cuts 6-5/8 inch crown from a 10 inch saw.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cut trim for a living. The Makita LS1219L or DeWalt DWS780 repays the cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cut occasionally. The Skil MS6305 or Dovaman is enough.

maintenance.why: Dust makes the head bind. A dry lubricant keeps it smooth.
A fence out of square ruins accuracy.
A dull blade chips and burns.
Lasers drift. Verify against a test cut.
A clogged port blows dust back.

faq.q: Do I need a sliding miter saw?
faq.a: Only for wide boards and large crown. A fixed saw suffices for trim. Always clamp long boards.
10 inch is lighter and cheaper. 12 inch cuts wider stock. A fixed saw is cheaper and simpler for small trim.

faq.q: How much space does a slider need?
faq.a: It needs room behind the saw for the rails, unless it uses an axial or compact design. Rails need cleaning more often than most owners expect.

faq.q: Is a cordless slider as good?
faq.a: For trim, yes. For long framing runs, corded is stronger. Cordless saws trade power for convenience.
A 60 to 80 tooth blade for trim and a 40 tooth blade for general cuts. Use a fine blade for finish cuts.

faq.q: How do I keep it accurate?
faq.a: Check fence and bevel with a square and keep the rails clean. Calibrate with a square regularly.
